# Finding ∫ -2·exp(x)·cos(x) dx

## Step 1: Identify the integral

I need to compute: ∫ -2·exp(x)·cos(x) dx

I can factor out the constant: -2 · ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx

## Step 2: Compute ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx using integration by parts

Let I = ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx

**First integration by parts:**
- u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

I = exp(x)·cos(x) + ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx  ... (i)

**Second integration by parts** (for ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx):
- u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx = exp(x)·sin(x) - ∫ exp(x)·cos(x) dx = exp(x)·sin(x) - I  ... (ii)

## Step 3: Substitute back

From (i) and (ii):
I = exp(x)·cos(x) + exp(x)·sin(x) - I

2·I = exp(x)·cos(x) + exp(x)·sin(x)

I = exp(x)·(sin(x) + cos(x)) / 2

## Step 4: Apply the constant factor

∫ -2·exp(x)·cos(x) dx = -2 · exp(x)·(sin(x) + cos(x)) / 2 = -exp(x)·(sin(x) + cos(x))

## Verification

d/dx[-exp(x)·(sin(x) + cos(x))] = -exp(x)·(sin(x)+cos(x)) - exp(x)·(cos(x)-sin(x))
= -exp(x)·sin(x) - exp(x)·cos(x) - exp(x)·cos(x) + exp(x)·sin(x)
= -2·exp(x)·cos(x) ✓

<answer>-exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x)) + C</answer>
